analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md: the date bump on line 3 and a new paragraph (head lines ~1287-1300, in the unseen later part of the file) describing ChunkBatcher/SendHandle/ChunkSender behavior. The supplied units cover head lines 1-805, which show only the unchanged date line and surrounding Nemotron Super and engine text. The added paragraph is documented only in the patch excerpt, which I examined.

No code, control or config change is in this PR, so no security regression is introduced by it.

The paragraph does describe a security-relevant property: ChunkBatcher.enqueue drops a frame when no session sink is bound, but the check runs when the enqueue closure executes. SendHandle and ChunkSender persist across reconnects, so a stale frame from an old request processed after a replacement sink binds would still pass the check. There is no request-to-session identity enforcement. The docs state this candidly.

This maps to the A-001 confidentiality and T-053 style concerns (stale state surviving a connection change). The frames are E2E-encrypted per request with a session key, so the realistic effect is likely misdelivery of an old request's ciphertext on a new session, which the coordinator would have to reject by request ID. I cannot verify that from the supplied evidence. The source files (ChunkBatcher.swift, SendHandle, CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift, ProviderLoop+Cancellation.swift) were not supplied. This is a documented existing contract, not a PR regression, so I report no finding. A later pass should check whether the coordinator drops chunks whose request ID is not bound to the current session or connection.

The canonical T-041 definition on the prefix cache does not conflict with the visible doc text. The Nemotron durable SSD checkpoint description is consistent with its encrypted, HMAC-keyed, TTL-bounded posture.
